event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Keurig Dr Pepper’s 2021 10-K squarely links the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic to multiple, material and already-realised risk vectors.  The disclosure moves well beyond boiler-plate: management states that the company “has been” adversely affected and itemises concrete operational, supply-chain, labour and cost impacts that have already reduced margins, delayed capital projects and inflated input prices.  The language repeatedly employs strong qualifiers (“materially”, “significant”, “have impacted our results of operations”) and ties the event to financial statement line-items (SG&A, cost of sales, capital spending).  While the filing also describes mitigation (monitoring protocols, policy adjustments), these references are generic and do not neutralise the central message that COVID-19 represents a present-day, high-severity threat that could further intensify.  Because the filing date (24-Feb-2022) is well within three years of the WHO pandemic declaration, the Time Decay Principle allows high scores.  Overall, the risk evidence is recent, specific and partly quantified, warranting generally high micro-scores that peak below the maximum due to the absence of detailed dollar figures and the presence of some mitigating language.

evidence_list.snippet: Widespread health developments and economic uncertainty resulting from the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemic to potential material adverse effect on business, financial condition and results.
Uses strong severity wording ('materially and adversely').
Event is ongoing and recent (0-3 yrs).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct statement of material risk tied to pandemic with strong language yields a high score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Our business has been, and may continue to be, adversely impacted by the response to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic in countries where we operate or our customers and suppliers are located, due to recommendations or mandates from governmental and local authorities to require vaccinations, close businesses, limit travel, avoid large gatherings or self-quarantine, as well as temporary closures or decreased operations of the facilities of our customers, distributors or suppliers.

components.reason: Acknowledges impacts already realised ('has been').
Details specific operational disruptions (mandates, closures, travel limits).
Projects continuation of risk ('may continue').
Recency within 0-3 yrs.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Actual past impact plus granular operational details drive a score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: Significant reductions in demand or significant volatility in demand for one or more of our products, as a result of, among other things: the temporary inability of consumers to purchase our products due to illness, quarantine or other restrictions, store closures, or financial hardship, shifts in demand away from one or more of our higher priced products to lower priced products, or stockpiling or similar activity, reduced options for marketing and promotion of products or other restrictions in connection with the COVID-19 pandemic; such impacts could further increase the difficulty of operating our business during the pandemic, including accurately planning and forecasting customer demand;

components.reason: Enumerates multiple demand-side shocks linked to COVID-19.
Uses severity adjective 'Significant' twice.
Highlights operational planning difficulties.
Event specificity and recency.
Forward-looking conditionality (could) not fully offsetting.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Rich detail on demand volatility and operating difficulty justifies a score of 8 despite conditional language.

evidence_list.snippet: Inability to meet our consumers' and customers’ needs and achieve cost targets due to disruptions in our manufacturing and supply arrangements such as the loss or disruption of essential raw materials or purchased finished goods, disruption of logistics, reduction or loss of workforce due to the insufficiency or failure of our safety protocols, or disruption of other manufacturing and distribution capability;

components.reason: Highlights supply-chain and workforce disruptions affecting manufacturing.
Links disruptions to cost targets.
Embedded within COVID risk section (event relevance).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Comprehensive operational risk within pandemic context earns a 7.

evidence_list.snippet: Failure of third parties, including those located in international locations, on which we rely, including our suppliers, bottlers, distributors, contract manufacturers, third-party service providers, contractors, commercial banks and external business partners, to meet their obligations to us or to timely meet those obligations, or significant disruptions in their ability to do so, which may be caused by their own financial or operational difficulties;

components.reason: Identifies critical dependency on third parties and potential failures.
Mentions international exposure increasing complexity.
Disruption could stem from pandemic-related difficulties.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Third-party failure risk is notable but less directly quantified, scoring 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Significant changes in the conditions in markets in which we manufacture, sell or distribute our products, including quarantines, governmental or regulatory actions, closures or other restrictions that limit or close our operating and manufacturing facilities, restrict our employees’ ability to perform necessary business functions, restrict or prevent consumers from having access to our products, or otherwise prevent our third-party bottlers, distributors, partners, suppliers, or customers from sufficiently staffing operations, including operations necessary for the production, distribution, sale, and support of our products.

components.reason: Lists multiple regulatory and quarantine scenarios directly affecting facilities.
Uses 'Significant' to describe change magnitude.
Covers both production and consumer access disruptions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Wide-ranging operational disruption scenarios tied to quarantine restrictions merit a 7.

evidence_list.snippet: All of these impacts could place limitations on our ability to execute on our business plan and materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

components.reason: Aggregates cumulative pandemic impacts to overall strategy execution.
Again uses 'materially and adversely affect'.
Highlights broad scope (business plan, financial condition, results).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Summative warning, though general, still material—score 6.

evidence_list.snippet: We continue to monitor the situation, have actively implemented policies and procedures to address the situation, and as the pandemic continues to further unfold, we may adjust our current policies and procedures as regulations or governmental orders are implemented or more information and guidance become available.

components.reason: Acknowledges ongoing uncertainty and need for adjustments.
Provides mitigating actions (monitoring, policies).
Indicates dynamic, evolving risk landscape.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Mitigation language substantially tempers the risk signal, leaving a low positive score.

evidence_list.snippet: The impact of COVID-19 may also exacerbate other risks discussed herein, any of which could have a material effect on us.

components.reason: States pandemic acts as risk multiplier across the enterprise.
Uses 'material effect' language.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Risk-multiplying effect acknowledged but not detailed; moderate score 4.

evidence_list.snippet: As this situation continues to evolve, new risks or uncertainties may arise that we are not aware of currently.

components.reason: Highlights unknown future risks linked to pandemic evolution.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic acknowledgement of unknowns gives a modest risk indicator—score 2.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and its resulting impacts on the global economy, particularly supply chain constraints and labor shortages, have led to inflation in input costs, logistics, manufacturing and labor costs.

components.reason: Specifies actual cost inflation already incurred.
Identifies concrete drivers (supply chain constraints, labor shortages).
Links directly to pandemic cause.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Clear, present and quantified-in-concept cost impact warrants a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced supply chain disruptions and significant inflation, which have impacted our results of operations in the current year and may continue to do so in the future.

components.reason: Confirms actual impact on current year results.
Mentions supply chain disruptions and inflation severity.
Highlights continuing risk into future periods.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past and potential future financial hits from pandemic-driven disruptions earn a 7.

evidence_list.snippet: In 2020 and 2021, as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, we have experienced delays in the construction of our new facilities and the production equipment contained within, and we may continue to experience such delays.

components.reason: Cites concrete project delays already realised.
Specifies cap-ex and operational capacity impacts.
Notes ongoing nature ('may continue').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Actual delays to strategic capital projects justify a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and its resulting impacts on the global economy have exacerbated employee turnover and led to labor shortages, particularly in the market for frontline employees in the production and distribution environments.

components.reason: Describes realised labour shortages and turnover.
Highlights critical frontline workforce exposure.
Directly attributes cause to pandemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Front-line labour shortages are immediate and severe, yielding a score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: The labor force has been and may continue to be impacted by a number of factors related to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, including government actions, such as vaccination mandates, unemployment benefits and subsidies, and laws and regulations related to employee health and safety.

components.reason: Identifies multiple external factors affecting labour supply.
States both current and future exposure.
Tied explicitly to pandemic context.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes policy-driven labour risks; moderate severity yields score 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Some of these items, such as the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and its resulting impacts on the global economy, including supply chain challenges and labor shortages, have led to broad-based inflation in input costs, logistics, manufacturing and labor costs.

components.reason: Attributes broad-based inflation to pandemic.
Specifies multiple cost categories affected.
Recent and ongoing.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Wide inflationary pressure across cost lines supports a 7 score.

evidence_list.snippet: Employee compensation expense and employee protection costs, which impact our SG&A expenses and cost of sales, are included as the COVID-19 item affecting comparability and are excluded in our Adjusted financial measures.

components.reason: Acknowledges discrete COVID-specific costs already recorded.
Links directly to SG&A and cost of sales (financial statement impact).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Explicit reference to recorded pandemic costs (even if adjusted out) provides solid evidence, scoring 5.
